questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of $12$ cm and a perpendicular height of $7$ cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a parallelogram $= b \times h = 12 \times 7 = 84$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: A trapezium has parallel sides of $8$ cm and $12$ cm, and a perpendicular height of $5$ cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a trapezium $= \frac{1}{2}(a + b) \times h = \frac{1}{2}(8 + 12) \times 5 = 50$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: The formula for the area of a parallelogram is:
questions.explanation: The area of a parallelogram is base $\times$ perpendicular height. Note that $h$ must be the perpendicular height, not the slant side.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has an area of $60$ cm$^2$ and a base of $10$ cm. What is its perpendicular height?
A trapezium has an area of $45$ cm$^2$. The parallel sides are $6$ cm and $9$ cm. What is the perpendicular height?
Why must you use the perpendicular height (not the slant height) when calculating the area of a parallelogram?

options.text: Because the slant height is always longer
Because the formula only works with the shorter measurement
Because area measures the space enclosed, which depends on the vertical distance between the parallel sides
Because the slant height is harder to measure

questions.explanation: Area is the measure of the enclosed space. Only the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides gives the true height needed for the calculation.
